snippet.title: How Many Billionaires Are There REALLY? 🤑
snippet.description:
www.magnatesmedia.com
How many billionaires are there? (more than you think)

~~~~~~~~~~~~~

How many billionaires are there?

Forbes says in total worldwide there’s 2,781 billionaires.

And combined they’re worth $14.2 trillion dollars.

However… there’s almost certainly more billionaires than we’re told.

A lot of billionaires deliberately want to keep a very private life, and so they don’t co-operate with Forbes to share any data. 

Or Forbes simply may not know about them. Forbes themselves admitted: ‘if someone sold their private business for $250 million in the 90’s, then they invested that money well, we’d have no way of knowing’. 

So this means there’s probably way more billionaires out there, we just don’t know about them. 


~~~~~~~~~~

snippet.title: What toys have kids played with throughout history?
snippet.description:
Trace the ancient origins of toys and games throughout history, and discover how play has evolved — and stayed the same.

snippet.title: Pennsylvania Baptist Pastor Stole $1.5 Million for Gambling
snippet.description: Pastor Gregory Collins was the beloved leader of First Baptist Church in Greenville, Pennsylvania for 15 years. He preached about integrity every Sunday, counseled families through crisis, and was trusted completely by his small-town congregation. But he had a secret: a devastating gambling addiction that led him to steal $1.5 million from church funds over fifteen years. Using fake invoices, forged checks, and manipulated accounting, Collins gambled away donations from widows, retirees, and working families at Rivers Casino and Atlantic City. When church treasurer David Morrison discovered the fraud in 2023, Collins confessed to everything. This is the story of how a man of God became a thief, how addiction destroyed a historic church, and how an entire community learned that even trusted spiritual leaders can hide devastating secrets.

snippet.description:
The story of Instagram is one of my favorite examples of lean startup principles in action... 

Imagine you created a company, and in 3 years you sold it for 1 BILLION dollars. 

That's the story of Instagram - and in this video we take a look at how ONE decision led Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger to create the company that we all know today as Instagram.

******

This is one of those rare startup stories that can be quite motivational to some entrepreneurs out there. But most importantly, there is one huge lesson that can be taken away from the insane story of Instagram:

KEVIN SYSTROM.
Kevin Systrom (one of the founders who created Instagram) was born on the 30th December 1983. As a child he worked at a vinyl record store, and was a big fan of the game Doom II (he was also an avid book reader, and still is to this day!). From Doom 2, Kevin found a love for computer programming. 

During his time at Stanford, he briefly met with Mike Krieger where they spoke about his experience on the Mayfield Fellows Program. Whilst on the program Kevin had worked at a tech company called Odeo, a company that later went on to become Twitter. You can find a lot of this information scattered throughout Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger interviews.

A MEETING WITH MIKE KRIEGER.
After finishing college and working for a few years at several companies, Kevin has a meeting with Mike Krieger (who was also in the area) at a café. In that café they discuss the ideas for creating their first ever app. But it wasn’t Instagram…

BURBN.
Burbn was a check-in app, much like Foursquare. This was the original idea that Kevin and Mike came up with before creating Instagram. 
Burbn received a large sum of capital from investors like Steve Anderson, and the venture capitalist company called Andreessen Horowitz. In total Kevin Systrom and Mike Kreiger had raised half a million dollars towards Burbn. But no matter how much investors throw at your company, it won’t change the fact that the market may still not like your product or service.
The sad truth was that Burbn was not getting much attraction. Mike and Kevin recognised this and realised they needed to change ideas.

THE PIVOT.
The Lean Startup by Eric Reiss popularised the term ‘pivoting’ for startups, and this is exactly what Mike & Kevin did with Burbn. They realised that most of their customers were interested in the photo sharing aspects of their app, and had little to no interest in the check in features. So they stripped away all of that stuff, and created an app that was all about photo sharing – some may have called this their minimum viable product (another popularised startup term from Eric Reiss’ The Lean Startup).

INSTAGRAM.
Kevin Systrom also went on a vacation around this time with his (now) wife Nicole Systrom. On that vacation Nicole told him that she would likely not use the app because she didn’t think she could take good enough photos. Kevin saw that she was trying to compare her own photo-taking abilities to her friends who would use filters on their photos. Kevin identified a problem immediately, and created the first ever filter on Instagram the X Pro II. 
You can still find the first ever photo on Instagram to this day on Kevin Systrom’s official Instagram account. 

SELLING FOR ONE BILLION.
Instagram was sold to Facebook for 1 billion dollars. The company is now valued at around 100 billion, and it can be argued that Kevin and Mike’s decision to sell Instagram was a clever one at the end of the day, allowing their company to grow at the hands of Mark Zuckerberg.

Bitcoin first began when a white paper titled “Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System” began to circulate on a cryptography mailing list. 

The white paper was signed by an individual going by the pseudonym of Satoshi Nakamoto. And to this date, Nakamoto’s identity has still not been entirely confirmed.

snippet.description:
This video takes you on a fascinating journey through the Top 10 financial crises in history — from the South Sea Bubble of the 18th century to the global meltdown of 2008. You’ll discover how debt, speculation, and human overconfidence have repeatedly brought entire economies to their knees. Through engaging storytelling and expert narration, we uncover the emotional and economic patterns behind every crash.

Each chapter explores a different catastrophe: the South Sea Bubble, the Credit Crisis of 1772, the Great Depression of 1929, the Oil Shock of 1973, Latin America’s Lost Decade, Asia’s 1997 collapse, and the modern financial disasters like the dot-com crash and the 2008 housing crisis. The goal is simple — to show how greed, euphoria, and lack of regulation keep returning in new forms across centuries.

This documentary-style video brings economic history to life in a way that’s conversational and easy to follow, even for viewers with no financial background. You’ll see how every collapse left its mark on the world — and what lessons today’s investors can still learn from them.

If you’ve ever wondered why financial bubbles keep happening or how crises shape our future, this deep dive is for you. Stay tuned till the end to uncover the common DNA behind all crashes and how understanding these patterns can help you stay ahead of the next big one.

snippet.title: Prisoners prepare for release and worry about an uncertain future | Inside The Women's Prison (3/3)
snippet.description:
As freedom looms for some and time stretches for others, one question lingers in the minds of the inmates in Institution A4 – will I be accepted? 

In this final episode of a three-part series, the women confront an uncertain future and potential rejection by their families, society and even themselves. Christeen, serving a life sentence, knows an upcoming review could change her fate but tensions with her cellmates mount. As Halen dreams of a future with a fiancé she has never met in person, Haziqah clings to the hope of reconnecting with her family during a long-awaited visit. For Joanna and Yuxin, the end of their sentences is within reach but their paths to freedom are far from clear. Joanna struggles with the possibilities of being abandoned by family and friends, while Yu Xin, determined to maintain her sobriety, faces her own challenge: her first job interview in years.

snippet.title: What is "The Thinker" actually thinking about? - Noah Charney
snippet.description:
Get to know Auguste Rodin’s infamous sculpture “The Thinker,” and find out who was the inspiration for this masterpiece.

--

Contrary to popular belief, "The Thinker" sculpture isn’t just a universal symbol of eternal contemplation. French sculptor Auguste Rodin intended it to represent a specific person— and fit into a much larger piece featuring the fiery pits of Hell. So, who was "The Thinker," and what was he actually thinking? Noah Charney digs into the secrets of this infamous work of art.

snippet.title: Crypto Genius Stole $8 Billion - The MIT Graduate Who Fooled Everyone
snippet.description: Sam Bankman-Fried was the golden boy of cryptocurrency—MIT graduate, math genius, billionaire at 30, endorsed by Tom Brady and trusted by Wall Street. He founded FTX, one of the world's largest crypto exchanges, and promised to give away his billions through "effective altruism." But it was all a lie. For years, he systematically stole over $8 billion in customer deposits to cover gambling losses at his trading firm Alameda Research. When FTX collapsed in November 2022, millions lost everything. Federal prosecutors called it one of the largest financial frauds in American history. This is the complete story of how the "crypto genius" fooled everyone—celebrities, politicians, investors, and millions of ordinary people—and how it all came crashing down, leading to a 25-year prison sentence.

snippet.title: Tom Petters of Minnesota: The $3.65 Billion Ponzi Scheme - And Everybody Loved Him
snippet.description:
Before Bernie Madoff made headlines, Tom Petters was running Minnesota's largest fraud. He owned Polaroid, Fingerhut, and Sun Country Airlines. He threw charity galas with governors. He lived in mansions and flew private jets. But behind the success was a $3.65 billion lie. For ten years, Petters convinced investors they were financing electronics deals with major retailers. The merchandise never existed. When his VP went to the FBI wearing a wire, everything collapsed. This is the true story of how a trusted businessman betrayed thousands of investors, destroyed legitimate companies, and got caught by his own recorded words. The American Dream turned into America's nightmare. Sometimes the people you trust the most are hiding the biggest secrets.

snippet.title: Corporate Corruption Documentary: The HealthSouth Fraud & Siemens Bribery Scandal
snippet.description:
This video dives deep into two of the most shocking corporate scandals in modern history — the massive accounting fraud at HealthSouth and the global bribery empire run by Siemens. Both companies created billion-dollar illusions that reshaped industries, destroyed reputations, and forced the world to question how far business ethics can bend before breaking.

You’ll discover how HealthSouth inflated its profits by billions through accounting tricks, the psychology behind executives addicted to success, and how Siemens built secret bribery networks to secure international contracts. Through six chapters of storytelling, analysis, and real-world lessons, the video explores the rise, fall, and transformation of these corporate giants.

This isn’t just a story about crime — it’s about the system that made it possible. Government oversight, compliance failures, executive greed, and globalization all played a part in enabling some of the most organized forms of white-collar corruption ever seen. These cases changed the rules of corporate accountability worldwide.

By the end, you’ll understand how both HealthSouth and Siemens became cautionary tales for the twenty-first century: proof that integrity, no matter how inconvenient, remains the most valuable currency in business.

snippet.title: Tracking Suspected Members of the Pakistani Taliban | Taliban Hunters (full documentary) | FRONTLINE
snippet.description:
Inside a counterterrorism police unit in Karachi, Pakistan, dedicated to tracking down suspected members of the Pakistani Taliban. (Aired 2015)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the nearly five years since the Taliban seized control of Afghanistan, there’s been a dramatic increase in attacks within neighboring Pakistan by the militant group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, commonly called the Pakistani Taliban or TTP. Pakistan has accused Taliban-controlled Afghanistan of harboring the group and enabling it to launch cross-border attacks, which the Afghan government denies — and in recent weeks, the fight between the two countries escalated into what Pakistan’s government called “open war.”

Against this volatile backdrop, FRONTLINE’s 2015 documentary “Taliban Hunters” offers relevant history on TTP and Pakistani security forces’ fight against it. This short documentary went inside a Karachi-based counterterrorism police unit dedicated to tracking down Taliban suspects. 

As the documentary reported, TTP first emerged in 2007 and used to have only a small, underground presence in Karachi, Pakistan’s largest city. But by the time the documentary aired, the group had been gaining ground in the city of over 20 million people, and carrying out suicide bombings and targeted assassinations there.

The film documented how the unit carried out raids to take suspected TTP members into custody. It also explored human rights groups’ allegations that Karachi authorities were abusing militants captured in the city’s fight against terrorism. Amid TTP’s current resurgence, “Taliban Hunters” is an illuminating snapshot of where the fight against them stood in one large city back in 2015, and how the group operated.

“Taliban Hunters” is directed and reported by Mobeen Azhar and produced by Jamie Doran. The senior producer for FRONTLINE is Dan Edge.

snippet.title: Why is getting bitten by a rabid animal so dangerous? - Charles Rupprecht
snippet.description:
Take a look at what makes rabies the most lethal infectious disease, and what measures you should take if you're exposed to it.

--

In 1885, Joseph Meister was bit in 14 places by a rabid dog. His mother rushed him to Paris for an experimental vaccine from Louis Pasteur, and he became the first rabies-vaccinated person to survive. Today, without proper intervention, rabies remains deadly in almost all cases. So, what makes it so dangerous to humans? Charles Rupprecht explores what makes this infectious disease so lethal.
